# daymath

> ISO 8601 calendar day math for JavaScript. date-fns-shaped function names. Temporal.PlainDate under the hood. No Date, no time zones, no silent local now.

## Links

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/daymath
- Source: https://github.com/leemr/daymath
- Playground: https://leemr.github.io/daymath/
- Changelog: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md
- Contributing: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
- Future / backlog: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/FUTURE.md
- Types: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/index.d.ts
- Implementation: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/index.js

## Install

```bash
npm install daymath
```

```js
import { day, addDays, differenceInDays, isSameDay } from 'daymath'
```

## Contract

- Inputs: ISO day string `YYYY-MM-DD` or expanded `±YYYYYY-MM-DD`, or Temporal.PlainDate from any implementation
- Range: `-271821-04-19` … `+275760-09-13` (Temporal PlainDate limit); outside it throws RangeError
- Outputs: ISO day strings (Temporal toString form)
- Date objects: TypeError on every public path including isValid(Date), except day()
- day(moment?, tz?): the calendar day of a moment, in a zone. Defaults are stated: moment is now, zone is 'utc'. moment accepts Date, epoch MILLISECONDS (as new Date(n) reads it), ISO day string, or PlainDate. A day carries no time so a zone does not apply to it. '11/12/2026' is refused. A lone string is a zone unless it has ISO day shape. Only export that reads a clock; only door a Date enters by. Never returns a Date, never stores the zone.
- isValid(badString): false
- getMonth/setMonth: 1–12 ISO (1=January), NOT date-fns 0-based; getDay: 1=Monday…7=Sunday ISO, NOT date-fns 0=Sunday; weekStartsOn default 7, 0 also accepted for Sunday
- differenceInMonths counts a month as full when addMonths would carry the earlier date to the later one, so 2026-01-31 to 2026-02-28 is 1; differenceInMonths(addMonths(d,n),d) === n always holds
- isSameDay is an alias of isEqual
- format only supports pattern yyyy-MM-dd (identity normalize); not locale display
- Intervals: { start, end }; areIntervalsOverlapping defaults inclusive false like date-fns

## When to use

- Pure calendar storage and math (hire date, trip day, passport day as strings)
- Swapping date-fns *names* while keeping string days (not a drop-in for Date-based code)

## When not to use

- Display formats like "MMM d" — use Temporal toLocaleString or date-fns
- Zoned times or instant math — use Temporal Instant/ZonedDateTime; day() converts an instant to a day but keeps no time

## PRs

Fork and open a pull request. Do not expect direct push access. See CONTRIBUTING.md. Keep 100% coverage on index.js.
